newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moroccan tomatoes to fly on Evergreen 747F.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan tomatoes to fly on Evergreen 747F.

text.p: Moroccan airline, Royal Air Maroc (RAM) said it planned to operate a Boeing 747 full-freighter service between Morocco and Canada dedicated to tomato shipments.

"We are currently finalising an agreement with U.S. company, Evergreen, for the wet-lease of a Boeing 747-200F which will operate between Agadir and Montreal," a Casablanca-based RAM official told Reuters.
The freighter service was scheduled to operate from November 21 until end-February 1997, the official said. Evergreen International Airlines is based in McMinnville, Oregon.C
"While we expect to operate one 747-200 freighter flight per week, our agreement with Evergreen allows us to add extra frequencies on an ad hoc basis if justified by demand."
In 1995, RAM had wet-leased an Air France freighter to handle tomato shipments, but this year none of the state airline's 11 747-200Fs were available, an Air France Cargo official said.

"Apart from the full-freighter operation, we also plan to ship tomatoes on our own 747 passenger services from Morocco to Montreal and also reserve some space on Air Canada's Paris-Montreal passenger flights," the RAM official added.
RAM's fleet of 737-200Fs will transport the tomatoes from Morocco to Paris.
RAM is working on generating cargo for the return leg of the Evergreen freighter from Canada to Morocco, the official said. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
